advisor_letter:
Marcus,

You and Tanya have built an interesting kind of plan — one where the savings portfolio and the rental properties pull together rather than against each other. Most reports flatten that distinction; this one tries to honour it. Eight years out from your retirement target, the question that matters most isn't whether you'll get there. It's how the two engines (the registered/non-registered savings, and the Hamilton plus Mississauga properties) sequence in the decade ahead.

The goals you've stated — a Muskoka cottage at 60, the broader couple plan — are present in the analysis. So is the tension every rental owner faces: real estate concentrates wealth and produces cash flow, but also adds capital-gains exposure at retirement and OAS clawback pressure if the income mix isn't planned. The report walks through the trajectory, the income picture, and the leverage points that matter most given your structure.

For any specific action — a sale of one property, the timing of registered withdrawals, or the cottage purchase — please consult a certified financial planner familiar with your full situation.
overall_assessment: The plan is excellent at **100 %**. The structural strength is the layered diversification: **797K$** in registered and non-registered savings, plus rental real estate generating cash flow alongside long-term appreciation — few profiles combine both engines this cleanly. The single zone deserving attention is the **11 years** of projected OAS clawback: it signals that the income mix in retirement will sit above the threshold consistently, so the lever shifts from accumulation to withdrawal sequencing and capital-gains timing on the rental side.
verdict: The dispersion between the cautious and favourable wealth paths (**372K$** to **1.2M$**) reflects normal Monte Carlo spread for an 8-year horizon — narrow enough that the central trajectory is highly likely. The favourable end at **1.2M$** suggests room to consider whether to consume more in early retirement or preserve more for estate purposes; both are viable from where you stand.
page_zero_verdict: You've assembled an unusual mix — financial portfolio plus rental real estate plus a strong household income — and you want a single read that ties all three together with Tanya in mind.
profile_summary: Combined household savings total **797K$**: **285K$** RRSP, **102K$** TFSA, **165K$** non-registered on Marcus's side; **142K$** RRSP and **78K$** TFSA for Tanya. Tax diversification is solid across the registered/non-registered split, and the **56.1 % equity / 43.9 % bond** allocation matches a balanced accumulation profile. The two rental properties (Hamilton duplex, Mississauga condo) add a third pillar that the financial allocation alone doesn't capture.
trajectory_insight: The central path projects to **663K$** at the end of horizon, with a cautious **372K$** floor and a **1.2M$** favourable ceiling. None of the percentile paths cross zero — the plan never depletes in the simulated range. The spread is driven primarily by equity-return variance over the 36-year horizon; the rental cash flow provides a stabilizing income stream alongside the financial portfolio.
income_insight: Government coverage sits at **33 %** of target spending, leaving a **$7,647** monthly gap to be filled from portfolio withdrawals, the rental cash flow, and Tanya's income mix. CPP dominates the public side at **$2,284/month** for Marcus and **$988/month** for Tanya. The rental cash flow becomes a meaningful lever — its stability through retirement will determine how heavily the financial portfolio needs to be tapped.
taxInsight: The lifetime effective tax rate of **22.1 %** reflects the broad income mix. The **11 years** of projected OAS clawback is the dominant tax friction — sequencing rental sales (if any are planned) and registered withdrawals to spread realized income across years would matter most. The optimized strategy already captures **127K$** in lifetime tax alpha versus a naive baseline.
estateInsight: Projected net estate of **1.2M$** after **168K$** in tax at death — primarily on RRSP/RRIF balances and unrealized capital gains on the rental properties. The cautious estate at **716K$** still preserves significant wealth-transfer capacity even in a poor-return scenario.
real_estate_insight: The Hamilton duplex and Mississauga condo together represent a meaningful portion of household wealth alongside the financial portfolio. Net cash flow contribution improves the income picture in retirement; the trade-off is concentration risk and capital-gains exposure on disposition. The decision of whether to hold both indefinitely or to sell one to fund the cottage purchase is the single highest-leverage real-estate choice in the plan.
goals_insight: **Cottage in Muskoka** at age 60 with a **425K$** target shows **95 %** probability — comfortably achievable within the central trajectory, with the median wealth available at goal age (**1.3M$**) substantially above the goal cost.
stress_interpretation: All six stress scenarios land between **96 %** and **99 %** success — the plan absorbs sequence-of-returns shocks (gfc2008 at **97 %**), persistent inflation (**97 %**), and even a 15 % spending increase (**96 %**) without meaningful impairment. The narrowness of these deltas confirms the plan's robustness comes from the income-diversification structure, not from any single component. Consult a certified financial planner for any specific action stemming from this analysis.
